description: This topic explains the meaning of and difference between a Prophet (Nabii) and a Messenger (Rasul), the mission and common qualities of the prophets, and the special status of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as the final messenger.

mcq.questionText: In Islam, what is the Arabic word for a Prophet?
mcq.explanation: Nabii is the Arabic term for a Prophet, while Rasul means a Messenger.

mcq.questionText: What is the Arabic word for a Messenger in Islam?
mcq.explanation: Rasul means a Messenger, one who is given a new message or law to deliver to people.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the main difference between a Nabii and a Rasul?

options.text: A Nabii is given a new scripture or law, while a Rasul only follows an earlier one
A Rasul is given a new message or law to deliver, while a Nabii may continue an existing message
There is no difference between them at all
A Rasul is only sent to animals, while a Nabii is sent to people

mcq.explanation: A Rasul (Messenger) is commonly understood as one sent with a new message or law, while a Nabii (Prophet) may be sent to uphold a message already revealed.

mcq.questionText: Who is regarded in Islam as the last (final) messenger?
mcq.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the Seal of the Prophets, the final messenger after whom no prophet will come.

mcq.questionText: What is one of the main missions of all the prophets?

options.text: To collect wealth from the people
To call people to worship Allah alone (Tawhid)

mcq.explanation: Every prophet was sent to invite people to believe in and worship the One God, Allah, and to abandon worship of idols.

mcq.questionText: Belief in the prophets is one of the:
mcq.explanation: Belief in all the messengers of Allah is one of the six pillars of Iman (faith).

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a quality that all prophets share?
mcq.explanation: All prophets are truthful (Siddiq); they never lie in conveying the message of Allah.

mcq.questionText: The quality of being trustworthy and reliable in the prophets is known as:
mcq.explanation: Amanah means trustworthiness; the prophets were always honest and never betrayed the trust placed in them.

mcq.questionText: How many of Allah's messengers is a Muslim required to believe in?

options.text: All of them, both those named and those not named
Only the prophets of one nation

mcq.explanation: A Muslim must believe in all the prophets and messengers of Allah, whether or not their names are mentioned.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is the name of a well-known prophet mentioned in Islam?
mcq.explanation: Nuh (Noah) is one of the well-known prophets in Islam; the others listed are not prophets.

mcq.questionText: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was sent as a messenger to:
mcq.explanation: Unlike earlier prophets sent to particular nations, Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was sent as a messenger to all of mankind.

mcq.questionText: Which title means that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the 'Seal of the Prophets'?
mcq.explanation: Khatamun-Nabiyyin means the Seal of the Prophets, signifying that he is the last prophet.

mcq.questionText: Why did Allah send prophets and messengers to mankind?

options.text: To guide people to the right path and away from misguidance
To make people afraid of one another

mcq.explanation: Prophets were sent as guides and warners to lead people from darkness and disbelief to the worship of Allah.

mcq.questionText: Which statement about prophets is correct?

options.text: Every Rasul is also a Nabii
No messenger was ever a prophet
Prophets were chosen randomly without Allah's will
Prophets did not need to worship Allah

mcq.explanation: Every Messenger (Rasul) is also a Prophet (Nabii), but not every Prophet was given a new message as a Messenger.

mcq.questionText: What did the prophets do with the messages they received from Allah?

options.text: They conveyed the messages fully and clearly to the people
They changed the messages to please the people
They sold the messages for money

mcq.explanation: A key duty of every prophet was Tabligh, conveying Allah's message to the people completely and faithfully.

fib.questionText: The Arabic word _____ means a Messenger who is given a new message or law to deliver.
fib.explanation: A Rasul is a messenger entrusted with conveying a divine message to the people.

fib.questionText: The Arabic word _____ means a Prophet.
fib.explanation: Nabii is the Arabic term for a Prophet.

fib.questionText: Belief in the messengers of Allah is one of the six pillars of _____.
fib.explanation: Iman (faith) has six pillars, and belief in the messengers is one of them.

fib.questionText: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is known as Khatamun-Nabiyyin, meaning the Seal of the _____.
fib.explanation: He is the last prophet, after whom no other prophet will come.

fib.questionText: The quality of truthfulness possessed by all prophets is called _____.
fib.explanation: Siddiq means truthful; the prophets never told lies in conveying Allah's message.

fib.questionText: The quality of trustworthiness possessed by all prophets is called _____.
fib.explanation: Amanah means trustworthiness; the prophets faithfully kept whatever was entrusted to them.

fib.questionText: The main mission of every prophet was to call people to worship Allah alone, which is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Tawhid is the belief in the oneness of Allah, the central message of all prophets.

fib.questionText: A Muslim is required to believe in _____ the prophets of Allah, whether named or not.
fib.explanation: Faith requires belief in every prophet sent by Allah, without distinguishing between them.

fib.questionText: The first prophet and first man created by Allah was Prophet _____.
fib.explanation: Prophet Adam was the first human being and the first prophet.

fib.questionText: The duty of a prophet to deliver Allah's message to the people is called _____.
fib.explanation: Tabligh means conveying; prophets were obliged to deliver the message fully and clearly.

tf.questionText: Every Messenger (Rasul) is also a Prophet (Nabii).
tf.explanation: All messengers are prophets, but not every prophet was given a new message as a messenger.

tf.questionText: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the final messenger and no prophet will come after him.
tf.explanation: He is the Seal of the Prophets, the last messenger sent by Allah.

tf.questionText: A Muslim may choose to believe in only some of the prophets and reject others.
tf.explanation: A Muslim must believe in all the prophets of Allah; rejecting any of them is not allowed.

tf.questionText: The prophets were known for lying whenever it was convenient.
tf.explanation: The prophets were truthful (Siddiq) and never lied in conveying Allah's message.

tf.questionText: Belief in the messengers of Allah is one of the pillars of Iman.
tf.explanation: It is one of the six pillars of faith in Islam.

tf.questionText: All the prophets called their people to worship many gods.
tf.explanation: Every prophet called people to worship Allah alone (Tawhid), not many gods.

tf.questionText: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was sent only to the Arab people.
tf.explanation: He was sent as a messenger to all of mankind, not only the Arabs.

tf.questionText: Trustworthiness (Amanah) is one of the common qualities of all the prophets.
tf.explanation: The prophets were trustworthy and never betrayed any trust given to them.

tf.questionText: Prophet Adam was the first prophet and the first human being created by Allah.
tf.explanation: Adam was both the first man and the first prophet.

tf.questionText: The names of every prophet that Allah ever sent are mentioned in the Qur'an.
tf.explanation: Only some prophets are named; many others were sent whose names are not mentioned.

hoq.questionText: Why is it correct to say that every Rasul is a Nabii, but not every Nabii is a Rasul?

options.text: Because a Rasul is given a new message or law while a Nabii may uphold an existing one
Because a Nabii is greater in rank than every Rasul
Because a Rasul never receives revelation from Allah
Because a Nabii is sent only to angels

hoq.explanation: A Rasul carries the additional role of delivering a new divine message or law, so he is also a prophet, while some prophets continue an earlier message without a new one.

hoq.questionText: How does the mission of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) differ from that of earlier prophets?

options.text: He was sent only to one tribe, like earlier prophets
He was sent to all mankind and is the final messenger, while earlier prophets were sent to particular nations
He brought no message at all
He allowed people to worship idols

hoq.explanation: Earlier prophets were generally sent to specific peoples, whereas Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was sent to all of humankind as the last messenger.

hoq.questionText: Why are truthfulness and trustworthiness considered essential qualities for all prophets?

options.text: Because people would not be able to trust or accept Allah's message from a liar or a traitor
Because these qualities make prophets wealthy
Because they help prophets win wars
Because these qualities are required only for kings

hoq.explanation: If prophets were not truthful and trustworthy, people could doubt the message they deliver, so these qualities are necessary for the message of Allah to be believed.
